_about: Hand transcriptions of the AENL226 Power Systems pages that are handwriting with no text layer (iPad exports). build_slide_index.py merges these into notes/index.json so search can find them. Keys are notes/<file> without .pdf, then the 1-based page number.

AENL226/PS-L2-3-system-modelling.5: Generation, transmission, distribution. Real power balance: sum of PG over NG generators = sum of PL over n load buses + Ploss total. Any deviation will be reflected in frequency.
AENL226/PS-L2-3-system-modelling.6: Single line diagram: generator, transformer T1, transmission line, transformer T2, buses 1 to 5, motor, load. Difference between power transformer and distribution transformer.
AENL226/PS-L2-3-system-modelling.7: Every device has capabilities in terms of active and reactive power. Loads described in terms of active and reactive power consumption.
AENL226/PS-L2-3-system-modelling.8: Components of a power system: generators (synchronous, induction, DFIG), transformers, transmission lines, loads (motors, heating, electronic loads), distribution feeders, voltage and power control devices STATCOM, TCSC, SVC.
AENL226/PS-L2-3-system-modelling.9: Synchronous generator: controls are possible, real power PG and voltage VG. PG is the input; field current If controls QG and VG. Independent P and Q control.
AENL226/PS-L2-3-system-modelling.10: Induction generator / motor: no independent P and Q control, consumes reactive power, used in small hydro. Load models R, L, RLC, Pload, Qload.
AENL226/PS-L2-3-system-modelling.11: Loads: load characteristic, P, Q, power factor. Frequency and voltage dependent load. Other types of generators: wind energy conversion system, induction, PMSG, DFIG.
AENL226/PS-L2-3-system-modelling.12: Doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) with AC/DC and DC/AC converters, grid frequency. Solar PV system: PV panel, DC/DC converter, DC/AC inverter, grid.
AENL226/PS-L2-3-system-modelling.13: 5-bus power system example: generator buses 1, 2, 4 and load buses 3, 5 with PL, QL at each bus.
AENL226/PS-L2-3-system-modelling.14: PG1 + PG2 + PG4 = PL2 + PL3 + PL4 + PL5 + line losses Ploss 1-2, 2-3, 3-4, 4-5, 5-1, 2-5. Representation of components: synchronous generator as a voltage source in series with an inductive reactance.
AENL226/PS-L2-3-system-modelling.15: Generators used in thermal, large hydro and nuclear plants are synchronous generators with independent P and Q control. Small hydro uses induction generators. Wind energy conversion system: induction generator, permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG), doubly fed induction generator (DFIG).

AENL226/PS-L4-per-unit.2: 5-bus power system: generator buses 1, 2, 4 and load buses 3, 5.
AENL226/PS-L4-per-unit.3: PG1 + PG2 + PG4 = sum of loads + line losses. Synchronous generator represented as voltage source in series with inductive reactance.
AENL226/PS-L4-per-unit.9: One of the ratings is selected as the overall system base. Generator 5 MVA 11 kV, transformers 11/230 kV and 230/13 kV, motor 13 kV. Per-unit values of individual devices are on different bases; equivalent circuits can be connected together only if all parameters are brought to the same base.
AENL226/PS-L4-per-unit.10: Equivalent circuit parameters are given at the rating of that device (data sheet or testing). Select a base MVA or kVA and base voltage, usually one of the ratings of the existing devices.

AENL226/PS-L5-component-models-bus-types.1: Component models: synchronous generator, transformer, short transmission line. Medium transmission line pi model and T model (T model creates an additional node). Long transmission line approximated by pi or T. Loads as R, L, C combination, Vs, Is. Solar PV. Induction motor as load.
AENL226/PS-L5-component-models-bus-types.2: Generator bus gives power into the network; load bus takes power out. Categories of buses: generator bus, load bus, reference bus. Pi = Pgen i - Pload i, Qi = Qgen i - Qload i (scheduled power). Bus data table: known and unknown P, Q, |V|, delta for gen bus, load bus and slack bus.
AENL226/PS-L5-component-models-bus-types.3: S12 = P12 + jQ12. Day-ahead forecast of generation and load, system operator balancing and dispatch. Safe operation checks: bus voltages within permissible limits Vmin <= Vi <= Vmax (0.9 to 1.1 or 0.95 to 1.05 pu), line and transformer power flows within limits Sij min <= Sij <= Sij max, e.g. 100 MVA <= S12 <= 500 MVA on 100 MVA base.
AENL226/PS-L5-component-models-bus-types.4: n buses: 2n variables known and 2n unknown, 2n equations to solve. Bus table |V|, delta, P, Q. Slack bus is the reference generator bus with delta1 = 0 and |V1| known, P1 and Q1 unknown, takes up the losses. Balancing and scheduling: sum PG = sum PL + Ploss (I squared R).
AENL226/PS-L5-component-models-bus-types.5: 4-bus system bus data. Gen-load pattern or scenario from the system operator. Topology and line data table: rij, xij, Bij/2 for lines 1-2, 2-3, 3-4, 4-1, 4-2. Ii = sum Yij Vj. Nodal analysis: nodal equation at node 1.
AENL226/PS-L5-component-models-bus-types.6: Nodal equations written in matrix form by inspection: Y11 is the sum of admittances of all branches connected at bus 1; Y12 is minus the admittance between buses 1 and 2.

AENL226/PS-L6-7-power-flow-ybus.1: Bus data and line data. Line table: start bus, end bus, r, x, b. Read data; algorithm for Ybus formation: for i, for j, if i == j Y(i,i) = sum of all admittances connected, else Y(i,j) = -yij. Ii = sum Yij Vj. Pi = Pgen i - Pload i real power injected at bus i, Qi = Qgen i - Qload i reactive power injected.
AENL226/PS-L6-7-power-flow-ybus.2: If Pgen > Pload then Pi positive (generator bus), else negative (load bus). Si = Vi Ii* = Pi + jQi; Ii = (Pi - jQi) / Vi*. Basic power flow equation (Pi - jQi)/Vi* = sum Yij Vj. Recap 10/09/26: real power balancing, reactive power balancing. Approximate transformer equivalent circuit (series reactance) is acceptable at power transformer level.
AENL226/PS-L6-7-power-flow-ybus.3: Transformer exact equivalent circuit with core branch Rc, Xm. Approximation: core loss current 2 to 6 percent of load current is neglected, xT >> rT. At low voltage levels (400 V, 11 kV and below) the full model is used; a distribution transformer's load varies through the day. Balanced three-phase system assumption.
AENL226/PS-L6-7-power-flow-ybus.4: Systems below 11 kV: 11 kV / 400 V / 230 V distribution needs complete three-phase modelling of each component, Y11 as a 3x3 matrix (detailed modelling). Synchronous generator can provide active and reactive power and control them independently.
AENL226/PS-L6-7-power-flow-ybus.5: Qgen controlled by excitation. Transmission line capacity in MVA, transformer capacity in MVA/kVA, S12 max = 500 MVA, S12 = sqrt(P12^2 + Q12^2). Power factor of loads at transmission level should be close to unity. a) Real power load-generation balance affects frequency. b) Reactive power load-generation balance affects bus voltages. Three levels of control.
AENL226/PS-L6-7-power-flow-ybus.6: Primary control (local, fastest; generators sense frequency change), secondary control (automatic generation control, coordinates generators), tertiary control (slowest). Planning load-generation balance day ahead. GENCOs (generation companies), DISCOMs (distribution), independent system operator. One day in advance: generators give availability, distribution companies give load demand.
AENL226/PS-L6-7-power-flow-ybus.7: Day-ahead scheduling table in 15-minute blocks (96 per day, 00:00 to 00:15 ... 23:45): generator capacity, available, allocated, forecast load demand. Total generation = total load + total losses + reserves (fast and slow). Tutorial 1, Tutorial 2, Ybus code.

AENL226/PS-notes-with-L6.2: Bus data and line data. Ybus formation algorithm: Y(i,i) = sum of all admittances connected to bus i, Y(i,j) = -yij. Ii = sum Yij Vj. Pi = Pgen i - Pload i, Qi = Qgen i - Qload i.
AENL226/PS-notes-with-L6.3: Pi positive at generator buses, negative at load buses. Si = Vi Ii* = Pi + jQi. Basic power flow equation (Pi - jQi)/Vi* = sum Yij Vj.
